701.author: qingkwl
701.body:
﻿## Problem

JiuwenSwarm (workswarm 0.2.6) pays a large, avoidable startup tax on every launch, which lands directly on the ScienceDiscovery desktop's "agent cluster starting" latency:

- the feishu SDK is imported up front even when the feishu channel is disabled (~4.7s);
- the AgentServer import chain pulls in pandas / pdfplumber / milvus (~6.8s before the server can even start binding);
- the heartbeat import chain (~2.8s) and the heavy `tui_connect` module (~1.8s) run before the ports are up;
- the Gateway<->AgentServer connect path blocks on warmup (~9.5s) and the post-listen warmup blocks readiness for another ~15.6s.

Same-machine A/B on gateway startup stage logs (Windows desktop line): warm restart ~17.5s without the fixes vs ~5-7s with them; user-perceived cold start 50s+ vs 20-25s.

## Proposal

We carry these as local patches today and would much rather see them land natively. The patch set (lazy-import guards, an off-critical-path preload for `tui_connect`, a shorter channel-config settle window, and gating the post-listen warmups behind the first request) is available in #700 as concrete, measured reference implementations — happy to split them into individually reviewable PRs against whatever layout the maintainers prefer.

| change | measured saving |
|---|---|
| feishu SDK lazy import | ~4.7s |
| tui_connect preload | ~1.8s |
| channel-config window 0.75s -> 0.2s | ~0.55s |
| heartbeat lazy import | ~2.8s |
| AgentServer import slimming | ~6.8s |
| unblock ws connect on warmup | ~9.5s |
| gate post-listen warmup | ~15.6s |

## Environment

Windows 11, ScienceDiscovery desktop packaging, workswarm 0.2.6, measured via gateway startup stage logs.
701.title: JiuwenSwarm startup latency: avoidable import and warmup costs (~35s per launch)

706.author: HugoXK
706.title: [Bug] CAS read() gives up after the first corrupt copy and never tries the other layouts

708.author: HugoXK
708.body:
### What is wrong

`packages/cas/src/index.ts` gives the two methods that have the same three-layout search the same first-path-wins bug that `#706` reports for `read()`, but the consequences are different and each one is a separate failure.

**`stream()` (`packages/cas/src/index.ts:108-124`) hands unverified bytes to the caller.** It opens the first path that exists, yields every chunk from it, and only then compares the running digest:

```ts
async *stream(hash: string): AsyncGenerator<Buffer> {
  for (const path of this.readPaths(hash)) {
    // opens path; yields every chunk; digest is checked after the last chunk
    if (digest.digest("hex") !== hash) throw new Error("CAS integrity failure");
    return;
  }
```

A corrupt copy in the current pool is therefore delivered in full and the generator throws only afterwards, so every byte is already out of the store when the error surfaces. The only caller of `CasStore.stream` in the tree, `materializeArtifact` (`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:20`), pipes those chunks into `publishWorkspaceFile`, which writes them to a temporary file, computes the size and digest, and then fails in `packages/cas/src/workspace-copy.ts:76-77` with `Workspace copy source size changed` / `Workspace copy checksum mismatch`. The temporary file is removed in that function's `finally` (`:106-108`), so nothing corrupt is left on disk — but artifact materialization fails (500 to the caller) even though an intact copy sat in the legacy layout the whole time, and the error names a size/checksum mismatch rather than a corrupt source.

**`retain()` (`packages/cas/src/index.ts:127-138`) refuses an intact legacy copy.** It copies the first existing path into the target pool and compares the digest of that copy only:

```ts
const target = await new VersionStore(this.dataDir).putFile(pool, path);
if (target.digest !== `sha256:${reference.hash}` || target.size !== reference.size)
  throw new Error("Legacy reference integrity failure");
```

so a corrupt current-pool copy makes promotion fail even when the legacy `cas/sha256/<first-two>/<hash>` copy is intact. `retain()` exists to promote legacy references, which is exactly the case where the object lives only in the legacy layout.

### Reproduction on `3fe9f9c9fca9e5c26ab8c53a3c15666823d3ab02`

Stored one 31-byte blob, corrupted the current-pool copy (`versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>`), left an intact copy at `cas/sha256/<first-two>/<hash>`:

```
stream: THREW after delivering 19 bytes -> CAS integrity failure
stream: consumer already saw: "corrupted pool copy"
retain: THREW Legacy reference integrity failure
```

Expected after the fix, with the same setup:

```
stream: delivers the 31 intact bytes from the legacy layout, no throw
retain: returns an object ref for the promoted intact copy
```

### Expected

1. **`stream()` never emits bytes it cannot verify.** Before yielding from a candidate, verify that candidate (for example hash it first, or hash while streaming into a buffer small enough to discard); on a mismatch continue with the next layout. If every candidate is corrupt, throw `CAS integrity failure` **without having yielded anything**.
2. **`retain()` tries the remaining layouts.** A digest mismatch on one copy is not terminal; it must continue and only throw `Legacy reference integrity failure` when every candidate it found is corrupt.
3. **Both stay byte-identical on the happy path.** Existing behaviour when the first layout is intact does not change: same chunk sequence for `stream()`, same target ref for `retain()`.

### Acceptance probes

- (a) corrupt pool copy + intact legacy copy → `stream()` yields exactly the original 31 bytes and no error; `retain(ref, "data")` returns a ref whose digest matches.
- (b) corrupt every copy → `stream()` throws `CAS integrity failure` with **zero** bytes yielded; `retain()` throws `Legacy reference integrity failure`.
- (c) intact first layout → unchanged behaviour for both, including the multi-chunk case for `stream()` (feed a payload bigger than one chunk).

### Scope and sequencing

- Same root cause as `#706`, different methods: `#706`/`#707` fix `read()` and must not be widened there.
- This fix touches the same function file as `#707` but sits in different functions; the branch is based on current `main` and will be rebased if `#707` lands first.
- `has()`/`verify()` predicates are out of scope (`#679`/`#680`).

### Environment

main `3fe9f9c9fca9e5c26ab8c53a3c15666823d3ab02`; `packages/cas/src/index.ts` blob `584cf1eaefc7ec9b5c4c2125de7bf13c39039ba0`. Line numbers are from that blob.
708.title: [Bug] CAS stream() delivers a corrupt copy before it can verify it, and retain() refuses an intact legacy copy

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: ebfd6b084d6c47d39c50227fadbd2150
Branch: dev1/fix/run-stream-turn-placement
Base: 0e7075c475fe
At: 2026-11-01T17:46:50Z

## Environment

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- live `main` sha: `0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba` (2026-11-01T17:05:39Z)
- Node v22.23.2; the desktop reducer is plain TypeScript and needs no Electron runtime.

## Reproduction (headless, no UI)

The desktop transcript folds a run's events with `reduceRunStream` in `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts`. The existing test file already has the helpers `fold`, `responseStarted(responseId, turn)` and `delta(text, responseId)`.

1. Add this test to `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts`:

```ts
test("a later turn's text is not folded into turn 1 when its response.started arrives late", () => {
  const state = fold([
    responseStarted("r1"),
    delta("first turn", "r1"),
    { responseId: "r1", type: "assistant.response.settled" } as RunStreamEvent,
    delta("HELLO", "r2"),
    responseStarted("r2", 2),
    delta(" WORLD", "r2"),
  ]);
  const second = state.turns.find((turn) => turn.turn === 2);
  assert.deepEqual(state.turns[0]!.responses.map((response) => response.content), ["first turn"]);
  assert.equal(second?.responses[0]?.content, "HELLO WORLD");
});
```

2. Run it:

```
cd apps/desktop && node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts
```

3. Observed on live main: `# tests 39`, `# pass 38`, `# fail 1`.

```
not ok 9 - a later turn's text is not folded into turn 1 when its response.started arrives late
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
        'first turn',
    +   'HELLO WORLD'
      ]
```

## Current vs expected

Current state after folding the script above:

```json
[
  { "turn": 1, "responses": [{ "id": "r1", "text": "first turn" }, { "id": "r2", "text": "HELLO WORLD" }] },
  { "turn": 2, "responses": [{ "id": "r2", "text": "" }] }
]
```

Expected:

```json
[
  { "turn": 1, "responses": [{ "id": "r1", "text": "first turn" }] },
  { "turn": 2, "responses": [{ "id": "r2", "text": "HELLO WORLD" }] }
]
```

The second turn's whole answer is drawn inside the first turn, and the second turn is left with an empty answer block.

## Code evidence

- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:366-382` — `withResponse` handles a `responseId` it has never seen by creating a turn with the hard-coded `turn: 1` (`const created: AssistantTurn = { ..., turn: 1 }`), for every event type, including one whose start frame will later announce another turn.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:107-111` — `assistant.response.started` adds a blank block to *its own* turn and does not adopt the block already created for the same `responseId`, so the same response exists twice.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:404-411` — `locateTurn` returns the first turn that owns the `responseId`, so after the start frame arrives every later delta keeps landing in the wrongly-anchored turn-1 block; turn 2's block stays empty forever.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:357-365` — the comment at `withResponse` documents this ordering as supported ("A frame that arrives before its `assistant.response.started`, or with no open response at all, opens a block rather than dropping the text").
- `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts:139-142` — the existing coverage is a single-turn orphan (`fold([delta("orphan text")])`, no `responseId`, no second turn), which is why this gap is green today.

## Why it happens in practice

- A frame that cannot be read is folded as `null` while its cursor still advances (`reducer.ts:88-96`, and PR #616 made that path explicit). If the unreadable frame is an `assistant.response.started`, its deltas are then anchored to turn 1 by the branch above.
- The same comment block says older records omit `responseId` on text frames (`reducer.ts:357-365`). Such a delta is routed by `locateTurn(state, undefined)` to the newest turn's newest block; when that text belongs to turn 2 before turn 2 exists, `withResponse` again creates `turn: 1`, and the subsequent `assistant.response.started(turn 2)` leaves an empty second block.
- Replay (`foldRunRecords`) reuses the same reducer, so a finished run opened from the desktop transcript reproduces the same wrong attribution, not just the live stream.

## Suggested fix (one file, ~10-20 lines)

In `withResponse`, remember a block created for an unknown `responseId` (for example a `pending` map on the state, or a block placed at `turn: 1` that is moved when its start frame arrives): on `assistant.response.started`, adopt/move the existing block for that `responseId` instead of appending a blank one. Keep the current single-turn fallback when no start frame ever arrives, so `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts:139-142` stays green.

## Acceptance

- The test above is added and passes; the file reports `# tests 39` / `# pass 39` / `# fail 0`, i.e. the 38 existing tests stay green.
- `node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts` in `apps/desktop`.

## Impact

The desktop transcript misattributes a turn's answer text to the previous turn and renders an empty answer block, and because tools and subagents are placed on the newest turn (`reducer.ts:146-196`), the transcript's step order no longer matches what happened. The same reconstruction feeds replayed finished runs, so the error persists after reload instead of being a live-only glitch.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues and pull requests: `reduceRunStream`, `run-stream reducer`, `"response.started" turn`, `"turn 1" transcript`. Results are the feature PR that introduced the reducer (#500) and the frame-error PRs (#505, #616); none of them reports or fixes the turn placement above.
710.title: [Bug] Desktop transcript folds a later turn's answer into turn 1 when a delta arrives before its response.started

712.author: HugoXK
712.body:
## Environment

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` `main` at `0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba` (2026-11-01T17:05:39Z)
- `packages/cas/src/index.ts`: `readPaths()` `:173-177`, `read()` `:102-122`, `stream()` `:129-146`

## What is wrong

The two methods search the same three layouts, but they disagree about what a corrupt first copy means.

- `read()` (`:102-122`) skips a copy whose digest does not match and keeps looking, so a corrupt `versioning/agent-state` copy does not hide an intact `versioning/data` one (`#707` / `#706`).
- `stream()` (`:129-146`) keeps the older rule: the first copy that exists decides. A corrupt first copy fails the whole call even when the mirror is intact.

Measured on the source, with one 210,000-byte object written by `CasStore.put()` (agent-state) plus `new VersionStore(root).put("data", bytes)` (intact mirror), then only `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>` overwritten with `corrupt`:

```
read(hash)           -> returned the 210000 original bytes
stream(hash)         -> THREW Error("CAS integrity failure") after 7 bytes
```

## Current vs expected

Current: `read()` and `stream()` of the same hash disagree — one returns content, the other refuses it.
Expected (this issue asks which one, and makes both follow it): either both fall back to the intact mirror, or neither does. The choice belongs with the maintainers; the code should not depend on which accessor a caller happens to use.

## Why it is reachable

`materializeArtifact()` (`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:20`) is the only `stream()` caller in the tree, and it fails the request when the primary copy is corrupt even though `read()` would have served the same object. `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts:64-66` pins the current `stream()` behaviour by corrupting only `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>` and asserting the request fails.

## Suggested test

In `packages/cas/src/index.test.ts`, one case that stores a blob, writes `corrupt` over the agent-state copy, keeps an intact copy in the other pool, and asserts that `read()` and `stream()` reach the same conclusion — whatever that conclusion is.

## Scope

- Not a duplicate of `#708` (that one asks for `stream()` to verify before it yields; this one is the accessor disagreement that `#708`'s fix exposed) or of `#706`/`#707` (those are `read()`-only).
- No PR from us yet: recorded, benched, and not picked up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.
712.title: [Bug] CasStore.read() serves an intact mirror that stream() refuses, so one object is readable but not streamable

Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 8a3e9527b33f4e999955db3b813f1bec
Branch: dev2/fix/workspace-upload-quoted-filename
Base: 84c81b806a527ce0a70dd63cbc004d7d5f5edc08
At: 2026-11-02T00:28:25Z

## Environment

- `main` = `84c81b806a527ce0a70dd63cbc004d7d5f5edc08` (2026-11-01T18:23:35Z)
- Node v22.23.2, Node built-in test runner; no local changes needed to reproduce.

## Steps to reproduce

Add the suggested red test below to `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` and run it:

```bash
cd services/api
node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts
```

Before adding it the file is green (`# tests 8 / # pass 8 / # fail 0`); with it:

```text
not ok 9 - readMultipartUploads keeps a quoted filename that contains a semicolon
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
  + actual - expected

    [
  +   'trial'
  -   'trial;phase2.csv'
    ]
# tests 9
# pass 8
# fail 1
```

A multipart request whose part header is exactly what a browser or curl sends for a file named
`trial;phase2.csv` is:

```text
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="files"; filename="trial;phase2.csv"
```

Running `readMultipartUploads()` on that body, then `uploadWorkspaceParts()` on the result, prints:

```text
parsed parts: ["trial","plain.csv"]      # second part: filename="plain.csv"
uploaded:     [{"name":"trial","path":"trial","status":"created"}, ...]
on disk:      ["plain.csv","trial"]
```

So the file is persisted as `trial` — truncated at the `;`, extension gone. The same line also
percent-decodes the quoted value: a part with `filename="100%25.txt"` parses to `100%.txt`, and
`filename="a%2Fb.csv"` decodes to `a/b.csv`, which then trips the basename guard.

## Current behaviour vs expected

- Current: `filename="trial;phase2.csv"` is stored as `trial`; `filename="100%25.txt"` is stored as
  `100%.txt`; `filename="a%2Fb.csv"` decodes to `a/b.csv`, `sanitizeUploadFilename` rejects it with
  `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, and because `uploadWorkspaceParts` rethrows that code the **whole upload
  request fails**, including the other files in the same batch.
- Expected: the quoted parameter is read to its closing quote (`trial;phase2.csv`), a plain
  `filename` value is used verbatim (RFC 7578 §4.2: only `filename*` is percent-encoded), and an
  invalid name fails only its own entry.

## Code evidence

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts:127`

```ts
const rawFilename = contentDisposition?.match(/\bfilename\*?=(?:UTF-8''|")?([^";]+)"?/i)?.[1];
```

`[^";]+` stops at the first `;` or `"` even when the value is inside a quoted-string, so everything
after a semicolon is dropped. The captured value is then decoded unconditionally by
`decodeUploadFilename` (`:143-149`):

```ts
function decodeUploadFilename(raw: string): string {
  try {
    return decodeURIComponent(raw.trim());
  } catch {
    return raw.trim();
  }
}
```

That decode is only correct for `filename*`; the plain `filename` parameter the browsers send is not
percent-encoded (`"`, CR and LF are the only characters the HTML spec escapes, as `%22`, `%0D`, `%0A`),
so a name that legitimately contains `%XX` is rewritten, and `%2F` / `%5C` turn into a separator.

The failure then reaches `sanitizeUploadFilename` (`:84-88`), which throws `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, and
`uploadWorkspaceParts` rethrows that code instead of recording a failed entry (`:348`):

```ts
if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH") throw error;
```

Existing coverage does not exercise anything but plain ASCII names: `readMultipartUploads keeps
zero-byte file parts` uses `filename="empty.txt"` / `filename="notes.txt"`
(`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts:87-111`), so the parser's quote handling is untested.

## Suggested red test

File: `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` (same helpers as the existing multipart test).

Name: `readMultipartUploads keeps a quoted filename that contains a semicolon`

```ts
test("readMultipartUploads keeps a quoted filename that contains a semicolon", async () => {
  const boundary = "----sa-quoted-name";
  const body = Buffer.from(
    [
      `--${boundary}`,
      'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="files"; filename="trial;phase2.csv"',
      "Content-Type: text/csv",
      "",
      "a,b",
      `--${boundary}--`,
      "",
    ].join("\r\n"),
  );
  const request = Readable.from([body]) as unknown as IncomingMessage;
  request.headers = { "content-type": `multipart/form-data; boundary=${boundary}` } as IncomingMessage["headers"];
  const parts = await readMultipartUploads(request, limits.maxRequestBytes);
  assert.deepEqual(parts.map((part) => part.filename), ["trial;phase2.csv"]);
});
```

A second assertion for the same fix: `filename="100%25.txt"` must come back as `100%25.txt`.

## Impact

- The stored workspace path and `originalName` lose the file's extension whenever the name contains
  `;`, so the uploaded CSV/TSV no longer opens in the table viewer and `inferMediaType`
  (`workspace-upload.ts:375`) returns `undefined`; provenance and the memory-graph `SourceFile` node
  record the truncated name too.
- A name whose decoded form looks like a path (`%2F`, `%5C`) aborts the entire multi-file upload
  instead of failing that one entry.
- Any client that quotes a filename containing `;` (browsers and curl do) is affected.

## Fix direction

One helper in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`: split `Content-Disposition` parameters with a
quote-aware scan (respect `"…"` and `\"`), take `filename` verbatim, and percent-decode only a
`filename*` value (`UTF-8''…`). No schema, route or desktop change; the existing basename guard stays
as it is.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues and pull requests for `form-data`, `Content-Disposition`, `multipart`,
`filename`, `filename*`, `semicolon`, `readMultipartUploads`, `workspace upload`: the only related
items are #606 and #506, which sanitize the name on the desktop side before it is sent, and #342,
which is about PDF parsing. No issue or pull request covers the server-side quoted parameter, and
`readMultipartUploads` has no hits at all.
713.title: [Bug] Workspace upload truncates a quoted filename at its first semicolon

719.author: qingkwl
719.body:
## Background

Measuring Windows desktop startup timelines (`python -X importtime`) on workswarm0.2.6 showed `jiuwenswarm.common.config` pulling in a full `portalocker` -> `portalocker.redis` -> `redis asyncio` stack at import time — **~1.00s cold, 95% of which is the redis asyncio stack** (portalocker itself is ~7ms).

```
import time: self [us] | cumulative | imported package
...
      25 |       6795 | portalocker
...
     972 |    999000 |   redis.asyncio.client        <- the actual tax
```

`config.py` is an all-entry import (every jw process — `app_agentserver`, `app_gateway`, `app` — imports it at module load), so this ~1s was paid by **every process, every launch**, even though:

- `update_config()` is a rare write path (uses `portalocker.Lock` only when persisting config changes)
- the same module-level `import portalocker` pattern is repeated in `gateway/cron/store.py` and `common/media_capability_config.py`

`portalocker.redis` is a wrapper that unconditionally imports the full redis client even when you only ever use plain file locks — so any module importing portalocker for file locking pays the redis tax.

## What we did (desktop line, patch 0017)

Three-file fix, <30 lines of product code:

1. **`common/config.py`** — `import portalocker` moved into `update_config()`; the lock dependency only pays on first write.
2. **`gateway/cron/store.py`** — moved into `_call_under_file_lock()`; only the locked store operations pay.
3. **`common/media_capability_config.py`** — the interesting one: `migrate_media_capability_switches()` runs at module load of every jw process. After the first run the `.env` already carries all explicit switches and `os.environ` has them exported, so the locked read-modify-write is a no-op. Added a fast path: if all `MEDIA_CAPABILITY_ENV_FIELDS` keys are already present in the environment, `return {}` — the process never touches the lock branch at all. The first cold run (or a `.env` missing switches) still takes the locked path.

## Measured Effect

Same-machine A/B on the Windows desktop installer line (f25 -> f26):

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| portalocker/redis in importtime chain (agentserver/gateway) | ~1.0s | 0 hits |
| hot-start gateway `run_entered` | ~4.8s | ~4.7s (R0, cold pyc) |
| first-start net (total minus wizard) | 33.3s | 28.1s |

The hot-start number is partially masked on machines where 360/Defender rescans fresh `.pyc` files (our R0 was all-cold bytecode); the first-start number (28.1s, full first-launch timeline) is the cleaner signal — ~5s of that comes from this patch plus the AgentServer construction re-chain of 0016 (AgentServer listen 13.95s -> 1.53s in the f26 field logs).

## Suggestion for upstream

Either of these would benefit any embedding product that imports `jiuwenswarm.common.config` at entry:

1. **Cheap**: move `import portalocker` into the lock-using functions (as we did — happy to upstream this as a PR).
2. **Upstream of us**: `portalocker.redis` importing the full redis asyncio stack eagerly is the root cause; if you depend on plain file locking only, consider whether `portalocker` is worth ~1s of every process's import time, or use `os.open` + `msvcrt.locking`/`fcntl.flock` directly for the file-lock use cases.

Happy to provide the three-file patch (diff against workswarm0.2.6, shipped as `0017-lazy-portalocker-imports.patch` in our desktop patch chain) as a starting point.

## Version

- workswarm0.2.6 (commit `70aa671`)
- Windows 11, Python 3.12
719.title: [Performance] portalocker import taxes every jiuwenswarm process with the redis asyncio stack (~1s cold)

721.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: f885e1e336b14b23b4ab7e6bf28554da
Branch: dev2/feat/evolve-gate-evidence
Base: 8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f
At: 2026-11-02T07:37:21Z

## What the user sees

An `/evolve` run finishes with one number, `bestTestScore`: the pass rate of the best candidate on the held-out gate shards. The run detail presents it as the evidence that the search made progress it did not optimise against. One evaluation of one candidate — with no evaluation of the baseline on the same cases — cannot support that claim. A run that wins 5 of 8 cases and a baseline that wins 5 of 8 report the same "improvement" as a run that wins 8 of 8 against a baseline that wins 3 of 8; likewise a 5/8 candidate that happens to sit on an easy split looks like progress. The payload carries no pairing, no n, and no verdict.

## Evidence on live main `8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f`

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/test_gate_domain.py:139-146` — the gate already computes `selected` (case → passed), then keeps only `cases`, the names of failed cases, and the rate. The per-case pairing a statistic needs is discarded before it leaves the domain.
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py:746-760` — `finish()` evaluates only `best.program.code` on `self.domain.test_shards` and emits `best_test_score=test_score`; the baseline program is never evaluated on those shards.
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/events.py:293-315` — `search_finished()` payload, observed by calling it on this tree:

```
search_finished keys: ['bestNodeIndex', 'bestTestScore', 'candidates', 'expansionsPlanned', 'status', 'stopReason', 'type']
has per-case evidence: False
```

- `packages/schema/src/evolution.ts:395` (`bestTestScore: number | null`) and `:596` (`gateScore?: number`) — the wire shape carries only point estimates.

## Red probe (fails today)

```python
from sciencediscovery_evolve import events

def test_search_finished_reports_paired_gate_evidence():
    event = events.search_finished("completed", 3, 12, best_test_score=0.625,
                                   stop_reason="budget", expansions_planned=20)
    assert "gateEvidence" in event, sorted(event)
```

```
E   AssertionError: ['bestNodeIndex', 'bestTestScore', 'candidates', 'expansionsPlanned', 'status', 'stopReason', ...]
E   assert 'gateEvidence' in {'bestNodeIndex': 3, 'bestTestScore': 0.625, 'candidates': 12, 'expansionsPlanned': 20, ...}
1 failed
```

The probe imports the evolve sources of `8bcc2237` directly (no new module is needed to see the gap; the acceptance test below adds the module the probe asks for).

## Smallest mergeable slice (one PR, Dev-2, <= 1 week)

1. New `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/acceptance.py`: `paired_evidence(baseline: Mapping[str, bool], candidate: Mapping[str, bool], alpha: float = 0.05)` returning `{wins, losses, ties, n, pValue, verdict}`. Exact paired sign test with `math.comb`; `verdict` is `"established"`, `"not established"` or `"insufficient"`; `wins + losses < 6` is `insufficient` (no rank or p-value is invented to fill the gap).
2. `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/test_gate_domain.py`: carry the per-case results out of the domain (`caseResults`, about 6 lines), reusing the `selected` map that already exists.
3. `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py` `finish()`: evaluate the baseline program on the same gate shards, pair the cases by id, and emit `gate_evidence` on `search_finished`; leave it absent (and say why in the log) when the run has no gate shards or the baseline cannot be evaluated.
4. `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/events.py` `search_finished()` and `packages/schema/src/evolution.ts` SearchFinished type: `gateEvidence?: { wins: number; losses: number; ties: number; n: number; pValue: number; alpha: number; verdict: string }`.
5. New `services/evolve/tests/test_acceptance.py`: 8-0 `established` at alpha 0.05, 7-1 `not established`, 3-3 `insufficient`, empty input `insufficient`; and an engine test where a positive point estimate with 5-3 reports `not established`.

Acceptance: `cd services/evolve && uv run --extra test pytest tests/test_acceptance.py tests/test_puct_engine.py -q`. The red probe above turns green, and no verdict other than `insufficient` is possible with fewer than 6 decided cases.

Smallest user-visible outcome: a finished run's result says whether the improvement over its own baseline is established at the stated alpha, and says `insufficient` instead of implying progress when the gate cannot tell.

## Caveat the implementation must keep

The exact sign test assumes the paired gate cases are independent. Cases from one suite can correlate (shared fixtures, one broken import, one flaky test), which makes the p-value optimistic. The verdict is evidence at a stated alpha, never a guarantee; a later change may replace the statistic with a cluster-aware one if suites show correlation.

## Deduplication

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `paired_evidence`, `gateEvidence`, `sign test`, `conformal`, `bestTestScore`, `evolution acceptance`, `test_shards` — no issue or PR covers per-case paired evidence for a finished evolve run. #567 is documentation for `/evolve` and #54 is the RSI direction; neither covers the acceptance statistic.

**Label note.** This account cannot write labels on the repository (403). Please add the repository's feature label when triaging; `agent-ready` was deliberately not requested.

723.author: HugoXK
723.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 964fdbe623a640019c6b9325759c2d3f
Branch: dev1/fix/723-escape-nested-window-guard
Base: 8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f
At: 2026-11-02T08:43:15Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f` (`test(launcher): cover unavailable Runner startup warning`)
**Area:** `apps/web` — memory-graph explorer vs. nested artifact viewer (CSV workspace / Mol*)
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Summary

Pressing **Escape** while a CSV workspace or Mol* viewer is open on top of the memory-graph explorer tears down **both**: the nested window and the whole explorer layer. The same interaction is already guarded in the standalone artifact viewer — the explorer is the only layer without the guard, and its embedded artifact modal is the exact place where the guard is skipped.

### Current behavior (file:line)

1. **`apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1051-1055`** — unconditional global close:

   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => { if (event.key === "Escape") onClose(); };
     window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
   }, [onClose]);
   ```

2. **`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:719-726`** — the same interaction with the opposite semantics, plus the embedded bypass at `:720`:

   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     if (embedded) return;                                   // :720 — bypassed inside the explorer
     function onKey(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
       if (event.key === "Escape" && !csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen) onClose();   // :722
     }
     window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
   }, [csvWindowOpen, embedded, molstarOpen, onClose]);
   ```

3. The two nested windows each bind their own window-level Escape and neither stops propagation, so one keypress runs both handlers:
   - `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx:156-168` — `if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();`, no `stopPropagation`.
   - `apps/web/src/MolstarWindow.tsx:129-133` — `if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();`, no `stopPropagation`.

4. **Reachability:** `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:872`/`:829` keep the CSV workspace and Mol* viewer mounted while `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:932` renders the explorer above the artifact section; the explorer in turn embeds the artifact modal at `MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1700-1715` (`embedded` on `:1702`). So "explorer open + nested CSV/Mol* open" is a normal state, not a corner case: open a dataset preview, open the CSV workspace, click "view in memory" (`:928`), then press Escape. In embedded mode the artifact layer's own guard is gone (`:720`), and the explorer's unconditional handler is the only one left.

5. **Same file already knows the pattern:** `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphTour.tsx:74-86` binds Escape in the capture phase and calls `stopPropagation()`, with the comment "it must NOT collide with the explorer's global Escape → onClose (which closes the whole explorer)". That guard exists for the tour only; the embedded artifact windows were never given one.

### Expected semantics

Escape closes the **topmost** layer only: with the CSV workspace or the Mol* viewer open inside the explorer, Escape closes that window and leaves the explorer mounted (selected node, filters, unfolded set and viewport preserved); a second Escape, with neither nested window open, closes the explorer. The standalone artifact viewer keeps its current double-Escape behavior (CSV/Mol* first, modal second).

### Impact

One keypress destroys the exploration state the user built: the selected node and its detail/artifact panel, the unfolded/scope-expanded node set, the active chain highlight, the search query and filter chips, and the canvas pan/zoom. The user has to re-open the explorer and re-drill to the same node, and the CSV/Mol* window they were reading is gone at the same instant. This reads as "Escape closed everything" rather than "Escape closed the window I was in".

### Verification plan (no DOM harness in this repo)

`apps/web/package.json` has no jsdom, happy-dom or @testing-library; tests use `react-dom/server` `renderToStaticMarkup` (383 call sites), and `tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx:25-27` states the canvas is "a WebGL island the SSR test harness cannot run". Two jsdom-free precedents apply:

- pure predicate extraction from this very file — `shouldFocusEntryNode` (`MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:736`) tested in `tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx`;
- source-text assertions for wiring, e.g. `tests/SidebarDrawer.test.tsx:75-80`, `tests/ProxySettingsEditor.test.tsx:154`.

Acceptance:

1. Export `shouldCloseOnEscape(csvWindowOpen: boolean, molstarOpen: boolean): boolean` from `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx`, returning `!csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen`.
2. New `apps/web/tests/MemoryGraphEscapeGuard.test.tsx` covering all three combinations: `(true,false)→false`, `(false,true)→false`, `(false,false)→true`.
3. Wire the explorer's global Escape effect to that predicate with the live nested-overlay state of the embedded artifact modal (the embedded modal already tracks `csvWindowOpen`/`molstarOpen` at `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:494-495`); any wiring that satisfies the observable below is acceptable.
4. Observable acceptance: with a CSV workspace or Mol* viewer open inside the explorer, one Escape closes only that window and the explorer stays mounted with its selected node, filters and unfolded set; the next Escape closes the explorer. Standalone artifact viewer behavior unchanged.

Red evidence on live main today — the module imports headlessly, and the guard does not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node --import tsx -e "import('./src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx').then(m=>{console.log('exports:', Object.keys(m).join(','));console.log('shouldCloseOnEscape =', typeof m.shouldCloseOnEscape)})"
exports: CHAIN_BUTTONS,MemoryGraphExplorer,NODE_LABELS,buildScopeChildCounts,countScopeChildren,countVisibleAndTotal,findArtifactNodeInGraph,findCodeNodeInGraph,findSourceFileNodeInGraph,mergeChainScopeExpansions,mergeExpansions,shouldFocusEntryNode
shouldCloseOnEscape = undefined
```

```
$ grep -rn "Escape\|shouldCloseOnEscape" apps/web/tests/
tests/ProxySettingsEditor.test.tsx:154:  assert.match(source, /event\.key === "Escape"/);
tests/SidebarDrawer.test.tsx:75:  // Escape closes the drawer, ...
```

No test covers Escape in the explorer today; `node --import tsx --test tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx` passes 6/6, so the harness and the predicate precedent are proven.

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search (`Escape in:title`, `escape explorer`, `memory graph close`, `MemoryGraphExplorer`) finds no report: the only Escape-titled issue is closed #672 (HTML entity decoding). Our open PRs `#311/#648/#658/#663/#664/#676/#678/#680/#709/#722` touch none of these files or handlers (#648 is the web test build, #658/#663 text truncation, #664 fetch guard, #676 desktop, #678/#680/#709 CAS, #722 evolve evidence, #311 evolve trigger).
723.title: [Bug] Esc closes the whole memory-graph explorer while a nested CSV or Mol* window is open

736.author: zhaochen39
736.body:
## Problem

The nightly real journey `J5` (shard `research-9`) failed with `locator.click: Test timeout of 600000ms exceeded` while reading the run timeline. Playwright had already resolved the first `details.timeline-disclosure.tool` summary, but the element never became visible and 1049 click retries consumed the whole test budget.

## Cause

A live run folds adjacent exploration steps into a collapsed `<details class="timeline-exploration">` (`apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx`). Whether that wrapper exists depends on the tool sequence the model happens to produce, which a journey does not pin. `test/helpers/journeys.ts` expanded only the tool card itself, so a card nested in a closed group stayed invisible.

The trigger is model-dependent, which is why it is intermittent: reruns on a local model that only called `run_shell` passed 4/4 and produced no exploration group.

A second gap surfaced in review: the region name is localized, and the two `zh-CN` journeys that call `expandToolStep` resolved zero regions, so the expansion was a silent no-op there.

## Fix

PR #735 expands the timeline's own grouping containers before reading or locating tool cards, matches both UI locales (`Agent activity` / `Agent 活动`), and caps a card-summary click at 30s so a future timeline layout change fails fast with an attributable visibility error instead of spending the 600s test budget.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `J5` passes repeatedly against the nightly model, including runs that produce exploration tool steps.
- [ ] `journey-first-run` and `journey-artifact-archive` (`zh-CN`) still expand and read tool steps.
- [ ] A timeline layout change fails a journey in seconds with a visibility error, not in 600s.

## Evidence

- Nightly failure: first summary resolved, `element is not visible`, 1049 retries, 600s timeout.
- Local DOM probe with the same structure: the nested summary is invisible while the group is closed, and expands/clickable after the group is opened.
- Local reruns on the helper: `research-9` planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1, twice (1.1m, 2.5m).

Refs #735
736.title: Nightly J5 can hang for 600s when a live run groups its exploration steps
